subject: Unexplained mid-cycle token surge — request for sampling export
messages:
From: Marta López <marta.lopez@quadrantai.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Unexplained mid-cycle token surge — our Nov 1 invoice

Hi David,

We're reviewing the November billing preview and see a ~38% consumption spike between Oct 28 and Nov 1 that doesn't match our traffic. We rolled out a streaming integration on Oct 27 (SDK v1.3) and tried to correlate, but our internal telemetry doesn't show a matching request volume.

Can you provide a token-level sampling export (timestamps, request_id, model, tokens_in/tokens_out, client_ip) around Oct 27–Nov 1? We'd like a short sample (a few hundred rows) first — if we can spot duplication/retries on our side we'll expedite reconciliation.

If this looks like overcounting on Redwood's side we'd appreciate a provisional credit applied while we investigate. Our account id is QAI-12345 and contact for PO/approval is billing@quadrantai.com.

Thanks,
Marta López
Head of Platform
QuadrantAI

[attachment: none]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marta López <marta.lopez@quadrantai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexplained mid-cycle token surge — request for sampling export

Hi Marta — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the surprise. We can definitely pull a sampling export for the Oct 27–Nov 1 window. To be efficient, could you confirm: 1) the specific project/namespace you used for the streaming rollout (the account id QAI-12345 is helpful), and 2) whether you have any request_ids you already suspect?

I'll loop in Ben from Billing to generate a CSV and Tessa from Product to flag any SDK-related anomalies for engineering. We'll aim to get a sample file within 48 hours. If we identify duplicated counting on our side, we'll propose a provisional credit and hold the disputed amount from the Nov invoice pending agreement.

Regards,
David Kim
Senior Account Manager — Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:07:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Unexplained mid-cycle token surge — request for sampling export

Ben/Tessa — forwarding QuadrantAI's note. Scope: pull sampled token-level records for QAI-12345 covering 2026-10-27 00:00 through 2026-11-01 23:59 PST. Fields requested: timestamp, request_id, session_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, http_status, sdk_version, client_ip. Start with a 500-row random sample concentrated on the spike period.

Ben — can you check metric for duplicate request_ids and share an initial % duplication estimate? Tessa — can you ask infra/serving if any batch window or retry logic changed with the SDK v1.3 push around 10/27?

Goal: response to customer with CSV + short summary and provisional remediation within 48h.

Thanks,
David

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexplained mid-cycle token surge — request for sampling export

David/Tessa — attached is a 600-row sample (see stub) and a quick analysis. Summary: we observed ~2.1% of request_ids duplicated in the sample window. Pattern looks like rapid client retries where the server accepted both requests (duplicate request_id with different timestamps) — likely caused by client-side retry logic plus a subtle race in our request de-duplication for streaming requests introduced in SDK v1.3.

Attachments: [attachment: usage_export_20261101_sample.csv (CSV, 145 KB)], [attachment: token_duplication_analysis_20261103.xlsx (XLSX, 320 KB)]

Estimate of impact on the billed tokens for Oct 27–Nov 1: ~+18,400 billed tokens attributable to duplicates. At QuadrantAI's Nov rates that equals ~$73.60. Proposal: apply a provisional credit for the duplicate-related tokens (we can calculate final amount after full export), and hold that line from the Nov invoice until we finish the full audit (target by 2026-11-12).

I've created HubSpot ticket QAI-12345-BILL (link below) and flagged engineering. Linking to drive export here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cEXAMPLE

Ben Carter
Billing Operations — Redwood Inference
[attachment stubs included]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marta López <marta.lopez@quadrantai.com>, QuadrantAI Billing <billing@quadrantai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexplained mid-cycle token surge — request for sampling export

Hi Marta — following up with the sample and our recommended next steps. Attached is the CSV excerpt and Ben's analysis (short version below).

Short summary:
- We pulled a 600-row sample for QAI-12345 covering Oct 27–Nov 1.
- We found ~2.1% duplicate request_ids in the sample; preliminary, not exhaustive.
- Estimated duplicate-attributable tokens in the full window: ~18,400 tokens (~$73.60 at your current rate).
- Cause: client retries + SDK v1.3 interaction with our streaming de-dup window; engineering has scheduled a patch for the de-dup boundary on 2026-11-09.

Proposed remediation:
1) We'll apply a provisional credit of $73.60 to your Nov invoice for the duplicate-related tokens; the credit will appear as line item "Duplicate request credit (provisional)".
2) We will complete a full export audit by 2026-11-12 and reconcile the provisional credit against final findings.
3) Engineering will deploy a server-side fix on 2026-11-09 to prevent the same duplication pattern.

If you accept this plan please reply with a confirmation and we will: a) apply the provisional credit immediately, and b) place the disputed amount on hold for collection until reconciliation. If you prefer a different flow for PO/accounting please advise.

Appreciate your patience here — we aim to remain transparent and keep production billing accurate.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Account Manager — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
